sources.entry: Websurfx ⚠ - Aggregate results from other search engines (metasearch engine) without ads while keeping privacy and security in mind. It is extremely fast and provides a high level of customization (alternative to SearX). AGPL-3.0 Rust/Docker

summary.one_liner: Websurfx is a privacy-focused, ad-free metasearch engine written in Rust that aggregates results from other search engines.
summary.what_it_does: Websurfx is a metasearch engine written in Rust that aggregates results from upstream search engines while aiming to respect user privacy and security. The README says it offers twelve default color schemes, support for custom themes via CSS, and search filtering across four levels. It includes multiple caching levels, a built-in ranking algorithm that reranks results against the query, and compression and encryption options. It has an experimental io-uring feature for Linux and supports custom proxies and Tor for fetching upstream results. Setup is described as possible with Docker or on bare metal, and it is configured through a config.lua file.
use_cases: aggregating results from multiple search engines
customizing search engine appearance with themes
searching through Tor or a proxy
notable: Written in Rust for memory safety
Twelve default color schemes plus custom CSS themes
Built-in ranking algorithm to rerank aggregated results
Custom proxy and Tor support for upstream queries
caveats: Only x86_64 architecture is supported at present, per the README
Requires a separate Redis server to run
README notes image search, categories, and quick apps are still missing
